accuracy.evidence: Checked against Development Matters 2021 (Understanding the World, 3-4 year olds: explore how things work, talk about the differences between materials and the forces they feel) and the KS2 Year 3 forces programme (a force is a push or a pull; compare how things move). Physics in the lab is right for this age: a push acts away from the person, a pull towards them, a larger push gives a longer roll before friction stops the car, a ball moves off in the direction of the push, and the adult text says energy added per push is what raises the swing.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years ideas: a push brings things towards you, every hand action is a push, a gentle push should go as far as a strong one, pushing a ball from the goal side, and pushing a drawer to open it. Each is a wrong card, a wrong park, a missed goal, a wrong job or a challenge option.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagshove has its own mechanisms: a push/pull card sort, a drag-back hand that sets a gentle, middle or strong push and rolls a car to a parking spot, a two-sided push that sends a ball into a goal, a drawer and PUSH-door that animate open and shut, and a swing whose height builds with each push. flagheavy and flagtower share none of this; the shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the rules by doing: a strong push overshoots the middle spot and the car is sent back with 'too far, try a gentler push', a push from the goal side rolls the ball the wrong way, a pull on the PUSH door is refused, and two gentle swing pushes stall below the star while two strong ones reach it.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong answers listed first: 'A push' for opening a drawer, 'A gentle push' for going further, and 'Left, to your hand' for a ball pushed from the left. The task straight after tests each guess and the done message says whether it held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions with ten tagged wrong options, each with its own message: a gentle push for distance or height, no push at all, pushing a drawer open, a ball rolling back to the hand, a rope tug called a push, and a tug called neither push nor pull.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the family readability limits; kid paragraphs are short sentences about a ball, a car, a rope, a drawer and a swing. Adult text uses the exact terms force, push, pull, direction, speed, friction, energy and the curriculum links to Development Matters and Year 3 forces and magnets.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed with no stock phrases. Each kid paragraph is one idea with an action to try; the adult paragraphs give the curriculum, the physics, named mistakes and what the lab does. Explanation overlap with every other lesson is under the 12 percent limit.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 light and 360x640 Android dark and light for every step: sort boxes now carry two-line labels that fit, the car and hand were moved in from the left edge after the first shot clipped the hand, the swing length is capped so the star stays on screen, and every button wraps below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs axe run found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone, and no console errors. Every canvas action has a labelled button (It is a pull, Give the car a strong push, Push the ball from the right side, Pull it towards you, Give the swing a gentle push) and the canvas aria-label reads each result aloud.
